obtained.how: open-access article (CC BY 4.0, per Crossref and the PMC record): full text from Europe PMC's REST service (fullTextXML for PMC13145305), one web 'page'

bibliography.checked_against: Crossref and the PMC XML front matter
bibliography.note: J. Anim. Ecol. 95: 824–836; epub 16 March 2026, print May 2026 (issue 5 per Crossref).

claims.claim: young-of-year pike ate as many roach in water stained to a visual range under 5 cm as in clear water
claims.source_value: Experiment 2: water colour had no effect on prey consumption across five browning levels (Abs420/5 0.02–3.06); the brownest treatment is described as giving 'a visual range of less than 5 cm'
claims.location: web page (Europe PMC full text): Results, Experiment 2; Figure 4 caption; Methods 2.2
claims.quote: In Experiment 2, water colour had no effect on pike prey consumption
claims.conditions: laboratory, 0+ pike (in Experiment 1, 24 fish of 34.5–79.2 g, ≈165–220 mm FL) feeding on 0+ roach (~50 mm FL), 9 °C, 5 or 10 prey per 700-L arena, 8 replicates per treatment (80 trials), humic acid added
claims.note: χ² = 4.85, p = 0.30. Consumption rose with prey density and pike mass.

claims.claim: perhaps because humic stain absorbs light rather than scattering it
claims.location: web page (Europe PMC full text): Discussion
claims.quote: Browning via dissolved organic matter, on the other hand, primarily reduces light intensity
claims.conditions: the authors' explanation, contrasting turbidity (light scattering, lower contrast) with browning
claims.note: The authors add that this 'may preserve short-range contrast' for sit-and-wait predators such as pike. Their wording is hedged, as the paper's 'perhaps' is.

claims.claim: the functional response of young-of-year pike is usually type II, but pike gave a dome-shaped response at 5 °C in clear water
claims.location: web page (Europe PMC full text): Abstract; Results, Experiment 1
claims.quote: In one treatment, 5°C clear water, the functional response was best described
claims.conditions: Experiment 1: 5, 9 and 13 °C × clear or moderately brown water (Abs420/5 0.020 vs 0.097) × 2, 5, 10 or 20 roach per arena
claims.note: The abstract: 'asymptotic Type II functional response under most conditions' and a 'dome-shaped Type IV' in cold clear water. The Results mention one apparent outlier in that treatment, and attack-rate estimates are 'associated with considerable uncertainty'.

notes: All three uses check. Useful for the model: the authors find 'strikingly weak effects of temperature and browning on pike feeding rates'. Their model gives pike a reaction distance of 1.5 m in clear water, 1 m in moderately brown and 0.5 m in heavily brown water, after Ranåker et al. 2012 for 0+ pike over Abs420/5 0.01–0.40. That is a better-sourced basis than the project's inferred reaction distances in §3.7.1.
